problem: Recruiting tools are fragmented across sourcing, review, interviews and scheduling; Lantern shares hiring context across agents that can run on or replace an ATS.
business_model: B2B SaaS; company reports $1M ARR in October 2026

founders.name: Thomas Chan
previous_startups: Two earlier recruiting startups with Justin Tang
founders.background_notes: Closed $2M+ in sales with clients including L'Oreal, Accenture and IBM per YC page.

founders.name: Justin Tang
previous_startups: Two earlier recruiting startups with Thomas Chan
founders.background_notes: Former Managing Director of AIESEC; three time Olympiad gold medalist in Informatics per YC page.

competitors.name: Metaview
competitors.what: Interview intelligence, added sourcing in fall 2025

competitors.name: Paradox (Workday)
competitors.what: Conversational ATS, acquired by Workday October 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi agent hiring workflows with integrations to ATS and interview analysis are standard but broad.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated hiring context creates some lock in; the market is crowded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Workday bought Paradox in October 2025; not yet observable for Lantern.

market_need_then: Company reports 30 percent month over month growth, 270 percent net dollar retention and clients including Hyatt and Crypto.com (company claims).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and emphasizes humans decide hiring

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Fondo blog and ARR Club; launched people.lantern.md for agents

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many unrelated Lantern companies.

outcome_analysis: Lantern AI reached a reported $1M ARR by October 2026 within weeks of its Fall 2026 batch, with founders who ran recruiting startups before. Outcome is open. Growth claims are strong, but the market is crowded and the name is generic.
